title: Fern and Whistle's Lily Adventure
markdown:
Fern the frog and Whistle the water shrew were the sort of pals who giggled so hard that pond water might come out their noses, if they had been so careless as to drink it while laughing. Fern was bright green, eyes like shiny emeralds, always wide with wonder. Boing. Boing. She could leap higher than a sleepy squirrel could climb, and her croak was a happy bubbly sound. Whistle was teeny-tiny and super-speedy, a nose that twitched and wiggled like a worm doing a jig. Squeak, squeak. He could tie knots faster than you could say pretzel, and he was speedier than a dropped crumb trying to escape a hungry bird.

One sunny afternoon they were splashing near the Giggleweed Patch, which really did make you snort-laugh if you brushed it, sending little puffs of ticklish pollen into the air, when a wise old dragonfly named Flicker buzzed by. His wings were stained-glass windows, shimmering with all the colours of a rainbow.

"Listen up, little water-lovers," he hummed, a sleepy lullaby of wings. "Have you heard of Far Lily Island? The most secret special place in the whole pond."

Fern’s eyes went wide and round. "Far Lily Island? Extra-bouncy lily pads?"

"At the very tippity-top of sunset, when the sky is raspberry jam and fizzy orange pop, a flower blooms. The Evening Bloom. Moonlight and giggles. It smells like blueberry pancakes fresh off the griddle and stardust."

Whistle’s nose twitched so fast he looked ready to zoom. "Blueberry pancakes and stardust. My nose is tingling." He did a happy dance, his whole body wiggling.

Fern did a super-duper hop that nearly sent her into tickly clover. "We must go. We must see it before it closes."

But Flicker landed on a tall blade of grass. "The Evening Bloom only opens for a blink of an eye at sunset. And Far Lily Island is way, way across the pond. You will need a super-duper speedy way to get there, faster than a frog can flick its tongue."

Therefore they looked at each other, grins wide as moonbeams. "We will build a boat," Fern declared, already imagining a big leaf for a tiller.

"Or a raft," squeaked Whistle, builder brain whirring. "A speedy raft. I know just the reeds. And big sturdy leaves."

They scampered along the pond’s edge and gathered the strongest tallest reeds that stood proud and straight, and some big flat shiny leaves that had fallen from the wise old Willow. Whistle wove and tied, tied and wove, little squeaks of concentration a happy soundtrack. Fern pushed and pulled with her strong froggy legs. It was a bit wobbly, a bit jiggly, but soon, standing proudly on the bank, was a magnificent little raft. They called it the Lily-Leaper.

"Ready, Whistle?" Fern bounced on her toes.

"Ready as I will ever be. Let’s go."

With a mighty push they sent the Lily-Leaper gliding. The pond was a giant shimmering mirror, blue sky and fluffy white clouds. Little water bugs no bigger than a freckle zipped and zoomed. "Excuse us, please," Fern called, tipping her head. The bugs giggled and darted. Zip. Giggle-giggle.

Then they came to a part of the pond where giant lily pads grew close together, like stepping stones. But they were the Wobbly Lily Pad Bridge. Each pad jiggled like jelly on a trampoline. Therefore Fern took a big brave leap. Boing. Wobble. Whistle scurried, tiny claws gripping the slippery surface. Scamper-scamper-wobble. They grabbed onto each other to keep from tumbling into the cool water. "Whoa there, slow down, wobbly pads," Fern shouted, doing a little happy dance to keep her balance. It was follow-the-leader on a very bouncy stage.

The sun began its journey down, painting the sky warm orange, soft pink, and a hint of dreamy purple. "Hurry, hurry," Whistle squeaked, paddling faster with a big flat leaf he had tucked away. His nose twitched with urgency. "We do not want to miss the bloom."

Therefore they paddled as if the pond itself were a race. A sleepy turtle blinked them right of way. A reed caught the Lily-Leaper for one heart-thump, and Whistle untied it with paws faster than pretzel. Finally, as the last golden rays kissed the water, they reached Far Lily Island. The biggest most velvety green lily pads they had ever seen, each one big enough for a picnic. Right in the centre, bathed in fading sunlight, a single enormous bud was slowly unfurling. The Evening Bloom.

It released the most wonderful smell, sweet and warm, like blueberry muffins just pulled from the oven, and sparkly, like bubbles in fizzy lemonade. The petals glowed with a soft silvery light, as if woven from moonbeams. A tiny moon, landed on the water, just for them.

"Wow," whispered Fern, big eyes shining.

"It is amazing," squeaked Whistle, his nose completely still for once. He usually twitched at everything. This was so beautiful he just stood there, soaking it in with his whole tiny body.

They sat on the soft cool lily pad, side by side, watching the Evening Bloom glow and shimmer. They did not need to talk. They had made it. They had shared this secret sparkly sight together.

As the bloom slowly folded its petals, as if giving a sleepy yawn, they knew it was time to go. The moon peeked from behind a fluffy cloud, making the pond sparkle with tiny diamonds. They hopped back onto the Lily-Leaper, hearts full.

"That was the best adventure ever," Fern said, giving him a friendly nudge. Her croak was full of delight.

"It really was." Whistle’s nose was already twitching toward the next escapade. "And it all started with a little bit of hurry, a lot of knots, and the best raft ever."

They paddled home under the twinkling sky. Splash-splash. Giggle-giggle. The Lily-Leaper bumped a reed and kept going, which was, Fern thought, exactly the right kind of ending for a pond.
characters: Fern (bouncy green frog), Whistle (speedy water shrew)
author: StoryGen Community
